output.title: Show HN: depsentry – behavioral dependency scanner for npm and PyPI
output.body:
I built depsentry to catch supply-chain attacks by analyzing what dependencies actually do—like new install scripts, maintainer changes, or unexpected network calls—not just known CVEs. It runs in CI, scans a 1,200-dependency lockfile in ~40 seconds, and comments directly on the PR that introduces risk.

We retro-analyzed the event-stream/flatmap-stream attack: depsentry would have flagged it 11 days before public disclosure. That’s the core idea: detect behavioral red flags that precede most real-world breaches.

It’s built in Rust for speed, integrates with GitHub Actions, and is free for open-source (already used by 300+ public repos). Current limitations: no GitLab support yet, and Python coverage is newer than npm.

Would love feedback on detection accuracy, false positive rate, and what signals you’d want to see next.
